topic: diagnosing linear, square and cubic scale-factor confusion
subtitle: Scaling an area by the square of the factor, scaling a volume by its cube, and recovering the linear factor from an area or volume ratio

traps.desc: multiplied the area by the linear scale factor instead of by its square
multiplied the volume by the linear scale factor instead of by its cube
used the square of the factor, the rule for areas, on a volume
scaled the area by the linear ratio instead of by its square
reported the volume ratio itself as the linear scale factor
took the square root of the volume ratio, the rule for areas

problems.desc: Open justification with a labelled sketch. A claim that doubling every edge of a rectangular box doubles both the paint needed and the sand it holds. The student must show that the surface area is multiplied by the square of the factor and the volume by its cube, so the paint quadruples and the sand becomes eight times as much, and must say why the exponent matches the number of dimensions being scaled. Read the reasoning and the sketch; there is no single numeric answer.
